A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Dr. DPO research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on IMDB, Anthropic HH, MT-Bench and Reddit TL;DR, including noise robustness, preference accuracy, win rates and sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds HH pointwise-noise results, KL-divergence measurements, a LLaMA2-13B comparison and generated-response examples.

M1.justification: The Dr. DPO objective, exponential pair weighting, gradients and roles of beta and beta-prime remain unchanged. The pseudocode in v1 Figure 7 and v2 Figure 9 implements the same procedure; the added toy example explains it.

E1.justification: IMDB, HH, MT-Bench and TL;DR remain the dataset/task coverage. v2 extends pointwise-noise testing from IMDB to an HH scenario with corrupted SFT responses and an unreliable reference model (Figure 3b). LLaMA2-13B is an added model configuration, despite being called a dataset in the text.

E2.justification: The retained comparisons preserve their comparator membership. DPO, cDPO, IPO and rDPO already appear in v1 Table 1. The new 13B comparison reuses DPO, cDPO and rDPO; WPO is discussed but not evaluated.

E3.justification: v2 adds a LLaMA2-13B evaluation and an HH protocol varying rejected-response inclusion during SFT while holding DPO pairs fixed. Existing training budgets, metrics and generation settings are retained. The clarified SFT-only corruption description for the original IMDB experiment does not establish that its actual protocol changed.

E4.justification: v2 adds targeted analyses of beta sensitivity under HH pointwise noise, whether performance gains accompany increased KL divergence, and two qualitative response comparisons (Figure 3b, Table 2 and Appendix E). The existing divergence, convergence, token-corruption and temperature analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies experimental run counts, seeds or significance tests. Existing shaded IMDB curves are retained without defining their statistical meaning; the new results do not introduce an uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: New result blocks substantially extend the evidence through HH pointwise-noise curves, KL measurements, larger-model results and qualitative outputs. v2 Table 3 reports 13B win rates of 63.67 for Dr. DPO, 59.05 for DPO, 53.52 for cDPO and 60.54 for rDPO. These are newly reported settings, not improvements over corresponding v1 scores. All five original numerical tables are retained unchanged.

T1.justification: The theorem statements, bounds, assumptions and substantive derivations are retained. Although v2 adds Appendix B.2 titled 'Formal Proof,' it recapitulates the existing RM-DRO/DPO derivation and robustness interpretation. Writing out the previously named variance also does not introduce a new mathematical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: interpreting DPO through DRO, relating beta to pointwise robustness, and introducing Dr. DPO for pairwise robustness. Additional experiments support these claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: v2 explains that zero artificial label flips need not mean noise-free data and adds an interpretation of gains without increased KL divergence. It removes the limitation that larger models were untested and proposes adaptive robustness tuning. The categorical KL claim overstates Table 2, which shows a small clean-data increase from 19.68 to 20.01.

D1.justification: Appendix C.3 newly details pointwise-noise construction: fine-tuned versus unrefined GPT-2 responses for IMDB, rejected-response substitution for HH, and unchanged DPO data. This clarifies previously underspecified implementation details. Existing hyperparameters, GPU information, pseudocode and code-access URL remain; detailed settings for the new 13B experiment are sparse.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds brief discussion of WPO and language modeling against worst-case topic mixtures. Both additions have unresolved '(?)' citations. Existing related-work comparisons and the identifiable bibliography are otherwise retained.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence remain. v2 revises parts of Section 3, reorganizes metrics and results in Section 5.1, adds explanatory walkthroughs, and moves limitations into the concluding Discussion. Author information and citation style change, and the generic broader-impact paragraph is removed.

P2.justification: v2 adopts the ICLR layout and substantially expands and rearranges displays. The original Figure 2 is split, the beta plot gains an HH panel, and new displays include KL and 13B tables, a noise-construction diagram and two qualitative comparison tables. Most original figures and tables remain with changed placement or numbering.

improvement.justification: v2 improves clarity and empirical support by documenting how SFT noise is isolated, testing that effect on HH, and adding larger-model and KL checks. The gains are limited by sparse 13B settings, unresolved new citations and the overstated no-KL-increase interpretation. The core method, substantive theory and original benchmark results remain unchanged.
